draft.title: Exploring llama-swap and Open WebUI as an Alternative to Ollama for Local LLM Management
draft.body: I came across a detailed account from a user who transitioned away from Ollama about a month ago, yet kept Open WebUI as their frontend. They now rely on llama.cpp or ik_llama.cpp for inference and use llama-swap to handle loading, unloading, and auto-unloading of models. The author mentions managing models and parameters through a large config.yaml file, which seems central to this setup. Interestingly, they highlight an improvement in model file organization, noting no more "weird location/names" and the ability to directly download models via wget from Hugging Face. Given these points, I'm curious about the practical trade-offs: How does llama-swap's model management compare to Ollama's in terms of ease and flexibility? Also, how complex is maintaining that big config.yaml, especially when juggling multiple models and system prompts in Open WebUI? Any insights from those who have tried similar setups or who have experience with model loading strategies would be valuable.
